subject: Request: Distinct SLAs for streaming vs. non-streaming endpoints
messages:
From: Sofia Almeida <sofia.almeida@acme.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Distinct SLAs for streaming endpoints — TTFT and sustained rate

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the streaming demo looked promising. Procurement asked us to confirm whether Redwood can provide distinct SLA commitments for streaming endpoints vs. non-streaming (batch) endpoints. Specifically, they want explicit Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec expectations per endpoint type rather than a single, uniform SLA.

Our requirements (high level):
- TTFT: target P95 under 300ms for streaming; want to understand if P99 is feasible for our higher-tier customers.
- Sustained throughput: 800–1,200 tokens/sec sustained for long-running streams (session lifetimes ~60s).
- Failure modes and fallbacks: how do you handle degraded cases (partial responses, fallback to smaller model, queued requests)?

Attached is a short PDF that captures the language Procurement wants included in the initial SOW. Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to: 1) define separate SLO lines for streaming vs non-streaming, and 2) grant an exception to the standard hosted SLA for streaming endpoints with clear success metrics and monitoring hooks?

We'd like to get a formal proposal this week so Sales/Procurement can move to signatures.

Thanks,
Sofia Almeida
Head of Platform Partnerships | Acme AI
Sofia.Almeida@acme.ai

Attachments:
- acme_sla_request.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

Subject: Re: Distinct SLAs for streaming endpoints — TTFT and sustained rate

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. I can confirm we can produce a proposal that separates streaming and non-streaming SLO lines with concrete TTFT and throughput targets.

Next steps from our side:
1) I'll loop in Product and Runtime Eng to propose concrete thresholds and risk language.
2) We'll attach a short latency/throughput baseline and a proposed amendment for Procurement to review.
3) If acceptable, we can route this into DocuSign with a limited-term exception (90-day pilot) to validate production behavior.

Can you confirm whether Acme expects 1) a universal P95 target across regions or 2) region-specific targets (we saw your traffic is primarily US)? Also, are the sustained tokens/sec numbers per session or per tenant? That affects capacity planning.

I'll be back with a draft today.

—Dylan

Subject: Fwd: Distinct SLAs for streaming endpoints — need engineering proposal

Team — forwarding Acme's request (below). Procurement is explicitly asking for separate SLO lines for streaming vs batch endpoints. They want TTFT P95 ~300ms (P99 if possible) and sustained 800–1,200 tokens/sec for sessions ~60s.

Questions we need answered for the proposal:
- What are realistic P95/P99 TTFT numbers for our hosted streaming endpoint today (global/us)? Please include expected variance during burst windows.
- For sustained throughput, is the 1,200 tokens/sec per single streaming session doable on a dedicated pod, or is that aggregate tenant-level throughput? If per-session is unrealistic, provide a recommended per-session target and a per-tenant burst SLA.
- Recommended fallback language: model downgrade (smaller variant), queued admission with 95th percentile delay < X, or region failover?
- Monitoring hooks we can offer (trace id, per-stream token rate metrics, per-token latency histogram) and how they map to SLA reporting.

I started a draft for Procurement to review (we'll convert to an Amendment): https://drive.redwood.com/s/acme/ACME-3921/sla-draft
Attached: acme_sla_request.pdf from the customer.

Please reply inline — need a consolidated response by EOD today so I can circulate an internal proposed amendment.

—Dylan
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Distinct SLAs for streaming endpoints — engineering proposal

Thanks for the ping — I've run the numbers and attached a short report (redwood_latency_report_q1.csv) plus a draft amendment (proposed_sla_amendment_v1.docx). Summary and recommended commit language below.

Summary (hosted, US region baseline):
- Current median TTFT (streaming) = 75ms; P95 = 210ms; P99 = 360ms.
- Current sustained per-session throughput we reliably observe on dedicated pools = ~950 tokens/sec for 60s sessions (P90), with an engineered ceiling around 1,200 tokens/sec for short bursts.

Proposed amendment highlights (recommendation):
1) Distinct SLO lines: streaming endpoints vs. non-streaming endpoints.
   - Streaming TTFT: P95 <= 250ms; P99 <= 400ms (US region).
   - Non-streaming TTFT (sync/batch): P95 <= 350ms; P99 <= 600ms.
2) Sustained throughput (per-session on Dedicated capacity):
   - Commitment: P90 >= 900 tokens/sec sustained over 60s on Dedicated pools (billing tier: Dedicated or Enterprise).
   - Bursts: short bursts up to 1,200 tokens/sec supported but not guaranteed for >10s.
3) Fallbacks and failure modes:
   - Automatic degrade path: model variant downgrade (e.g., redwood-medium) with prior notice and objective-quality threshold (internal eval).
   - Queue-based admission: when capacity constrained, we offer queued admission with P95 admission delay < 5s for Dedicated customers; Hosted customers may see higher delays.
4) Monitoring & reporting:
   - Per-request trace ids included (x-rd-trace) and per-stream token-rate histograms available via Console with 30d retention (add-on option for 90d).
5) Pilot term:
   - 90-day pilot exception where SLA metrics will be validated against real traffic; at pilot end, we can re-evaluate commitments and scale Dedicated capacity if required.

Risks / Notes:
- P99 for streaming at <300ms is aggressive at global scale; we can offer US-region P99 <= 400ms as above.
- Sustained >1,000 tokens/sec per session starts to require dedicated capacity and careful batching knobs; we'll include configuration recommendations (token chunking, kv-cache sizing).

Attached are the CSV latency samples and the draft amendment. If legal/procurement want different wording, we can iterate — but this gives a concrete starting point.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Runtime Engineering | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Proposed amendment for streaming SLAs (initial)

Hi Sofia — appreciate the patience. Attached is our initial amendment and a short latency baseline showing US-region numbers. Key points:

- We can and will define separate SLO lines for streaming vs. non-streaming endpoints.
- Proposed commit for streaming TTFT: P95 <= 250ms; P99 <= 400ms (US).
- Proposed sustained per-session throughput (Dedicated): P90 >= 900 tokens/sec over 60s; short bursts up to 1,200 tokens/sec (not guaranteed beyond 10s).
- We recommend a 90-day pilot exception so we can validate against your production traffic and tune autoscaling/batching settings.

What we need from Acme to proceed to DocuSign:
1) Confirm whether you want the commitment applied to Hosted or only Dedicated. Our recommendation is Dedicated for the sustained throughput numbers.
2) Confirm whether region-specific P99s are required (we offered US-region numbers above).
3) Sign off on the pilot exception period and monitoring/reporting cadence.

If you're comfortable, we'll generate a DocuSign with the amendment and pilot terms. Linking the draft here: https://drive.redwood.com/s/acme/ACME-3921/sla-draft

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the metrics and risk language.

Best,
